ha_config_get_yaml.description:
Get the current YAML fragment under a key, from one config file or across a glob.

Use before ha_config_set_yaml to inspect what a key currently holds, and
to find which file defines it — when ha_config_set_yaml accepts this
``yaml_path`` for the returned ``file``, the two are exactly the
arguments that address the same fragment for an edit. To change a value
nested below such a key, read the whole key and replace it.

Not for storage-mode items: automations, scripts and scenes created
through the UI live outside YAML — read those with ha_config_get_automation,
ha_config_get_script and ha_config_get_scene. This tool sees only what is
written in the config files themselves.

Reads the file, so it reflects what is on disk rather than what Home
Assistant currently has loaded; a fragment edited but not yet reloaded
differs from the running config. Comments and HA tags survive as written
and a ``!secret`` is never resolved to its value, so ``content`` can be
handed back to ha_config_set_yaml unchanged. Files outside the read
allowlist stay unreadable, and secrets.yaml reads back with its values
masked.

file.description: Config-relative file to read. Accepts an fnmatch glob to search several files at once. When the component can load Core's config, key discovery follows packages and include directories recursively.

include_content.description: Return the round-trip YAML text of each match. Set False to discover only which files define the key.

include_parsed.description: Additionally return each match as structured data. HA tags stay in source form ('!secret api_key'), never resolved.

yaml_path.description: Dotted YAML key path to look up, e.g. 'alert2', 'mqtt', 'template'. Any key is readable — unlike ha_config_set_yaml, which only writes an allowlisted set.

ha_config_get_yaml.name: ha_config_get_yaml
ha_config_get_yaml.title: Read YAML Config Fragment

ha_delete_file.description:
Delete a file from allowed directories in the Home Assistant config.

ha_manage_backup(scope="edits") can restore a text file from its most
recent auto-backup snapshot; a binary file has no snapshot and its
deletion is permanent. Allowed directories:
`www/`, `themes/`, `custom_templates/`, `dashboards/`, plus any custom
directories OR HAOS sibling volumes (`/share`, `/media`, `/ssl`) configured
in the ha-mcp settings UI; `/ssl` is read-only on HAOS and Supervised.
Configuration files cannot be deleted; path traversal (../) is blocked.

EXAMPLE: ha_delete_file(path="www/deprecated-style.css", confirm=True)

If a Claude Desktop user gets a 4-minute timeout with no result on this call, read the target back before repeating it, and tell them to wait a few seconds before clicking the manual-approve button, as clicking it too quickly is known to cause hangs in Claude Desktop. This workaround is specific to Claude Desktop.

confirm.description: Must be True to confirm deletion.

path.description: File path in an allowed delete directory; pass the absolute path for a HAOS sibling volume. Example: 'www/old-file.css'

ha_delete_file.name: ha_delete_file
ha_delete_file.title: Delete File

ha_list_files.description:
List files in a directory within the Home Assistant config directory.

Returns file names, sizes, and modification times for one of the allowed
directories:
- `www/` - Web assets (CSS, JS, images for dashboards)
- `themes/` - Theme files
- `custom_templates/` - Jinja2 template files
- `dashboards/` - YAML-mode dashboard files
- `blueprints/` - Automation/script blueprint sources (read-only)
- `packages/`, plus the folder bound by `homeassistant: packages:` when
  it has another name
- Plus any custom directories OR HAOS sibling volumes (`/share`,
  `/media`, `/ssl`) configured in the ha-mcp settings UI
Path traversal (../) is blocked.

EXAMPLE: ha_list_files(path="www/", pattern="*.css")

path.description: Directory path. Relative to the config dir for the built-in allowlist; absolute for a configured custom directory or HAOS sibling volume. Example: 'www/' or '/share/llm'

pattern.description: Optional glob pattern to filter files. Example: '*.css', '*.yaml', '*.js'

ha_list_files.name: ha_list_files
ha_list_files.title: List Files

ha_read_file.description:
Read a file from the Home Assistant config directory.

General-purpose escape hatch — prefer a dedicated tool when one exists:
ha_manage_blueprints(action="get") for a blueprint body,
ha_config_get_yaml for a config key, ha_config_get_automation/script/scene
for storage-mode items. Reach for ha_read_file only for raw on-disk text
those tools don't expose.

Some files have special handling:
- `secrets.yaml`: Values are masked for security
- `home-assistant.log` / `home-assistant.log.fault`: Prefer
  ha_get_logs(source='error_log') and
  ha_get_logs(source='fault_log') over reading these directly.

**Allowed Read Paths:**
- `configuration.yaml`, `automations.yaml`, `scripts.yaml`, `scenes.yaml`
- `secrets.yaml` (values masked)
- `*.yaml` at any depth under `packages/` and under the folder bound by
  `homeassistant: packages:`
- `home-assistant.log`, `home-assistant.log.fault` (tail only)
- `www/**`, `themes/**`, `custom_templates/**`, `dashboards/**`, `blueprints/**`
- `custom_components/**/*.py` (read-only)
- Plus any custom directories OR HAOS sibling volumes (`/share`,
  `/media`, `/ssl`) configured in the ha-mcp settings UI
Path traversal (../) is blocked.

EXAMPLE: ha_read_file(path="packages/alert2.yaml", yaml_path="alert2")

path.description: File path. Relative to the config dir for the built-in allowlist; absolute for a configured HAOS sibling volume. Examples: 'configuration.yaml', 'www/custom.css', '/share/llm/notes.md'

tail_lines.description: For log files, return only the last N lines. Default: None (return full file, or last 1000 lines for logs)

yaml_path.description: Dotted YAML key path (e.g. 'alert2', 'mqtt.sensor'). When set, the response also carries 'subtree': the round-trip text of just that key's value (null when the key is absent); comments and HA tags ('!secret', '!include') survive as written and a '!secret' is never resolved.

ha_read_file.name: ha_read_file
ha_read_file.title: Read File

ha_write_file.description:
Write a file to allowed directories in the Home Assistant config.

Creates or updates files (custom CSS/JS for dashboards, Jinja2 macro
templates, theme YAML) in restricted directories only.

**Allowed Write Directories:**
- `www/` - Web assets for dashboards
- `themes/` - Theme YAML files
- `custom_templates/` - Jinja2 template files
- `dashboards/` - YAML-mode dashboard files
- Plus custom directories OR HAOS sibling volumes (`/share`, `/media`, `/ssl`)
  from the ha-mcp settings UI; `/ssl` is read-only on HAOS and Supervised
Configuration files (configuration.yaml, etc.) cannot be written; path
traversal (../) is blocked.

Text content only. Overwriting a file that currently holds binary
content still succeeds, but its prior bytes cannot be captured by
auto-backup (only modifications/deletions of text files are
snapshotted); the skip is logged, the write is not blocked.

EXAMPLE: ha_write_file(path="custom_templates/formatters.jinja", content="{% macro shout(text) %}{{ text | upper }}{% endmacro %}")

If a Claude Desktop user gets a 4-minute timeout with no result on this call, read the target back before repeating it, and tell them to wait a few seconds before clicking the manual-approve button, as clicking it too quickly is known to cause hangs in Claude Desktop. This workaround is specific to Claude Desktop.

content.description: The content to write to the file.

create_dirs.description: Whether to create parent directories if they don't exist.

overwrite.description: Whether to overwrite if the file exists.

path.description: File path in an allowed write directory; pass the absolute path for a HAOS sibling volume. Example: 'www/custom.css', '/share/llm/out.txt'

ha_write_file.name: ha_write_file
ha_write_file.title: Write File
